text:
sasha: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's continuous-batching coalescer tweak I'm seeing steady memory growth on long-context (50k+) smoke runs. Not immediate, but cumulative over ~10k tokens.

ravinder: ugh. is this the split/merge path change that avoids small-batch flushing?

sasha: yes. we started coalescing adjacent batches more aggressively to reduce tiny-batch overhead. perf looked great for throughput but KV residency climbs.

marta: any repro? stack/profile info?

sasha: repro is pretty consistent on local perf instance. sequence: run chat-dialog with 60k rolling context, continuous batching enabled, coalesce_threshold=3. After ~200 requests memory increases ~30-40MB per request until eviction pressure spikes.

oliver: can you paste the heap diff / alloc trace? suspect fragmentation + repeated allocation of new KV fragments instead of reusing slot pool.

sasha: pasted small snippet from allocator traces: ```
alloc KVFrag 0x7f8a3c000 size=524288 epoch=1023
free KVFrag 0x7f8a3c000
alloc KVFrag 0x7f8a3f000 size=524288 epoch=1024
alloc KVFrag 0x7f8a42000 size=524288 epoch=1025
// old frag freed but not returned to reuse pool, new ones allocated
```

ravinder: that pattern smells like reuse map key mismatch when batches merge — we change the batch id and can't find an existing frag in the reuse table so we allocate.

sasha: exactly. merging two in-flight batches results in a new synthetic batch token, and our reuse-index uses exact batch-key (batch_id, seq_start). When merge happens we don't translate old keys -> merged key.

marta: consequence is fragmentation: small gaps in KV table that kernels still treat as reserved, plus more pressure on the pager/evictor. Does evictor run more aggressively?

sasha: yes. eviction triggers, but we see repeated page-in/out churn and head-of-line blocking — some long-running request waits while others get merged and cause pointer reshuffle. p99 latency spikes.

infra-bot: deploy bot: rolling deploy of coalescer v2 succeeded at 12:03 UTC.

oliver: any profiling showing CPU hotspot?
sasha: perf top shows memcpy and a lot of time in "copy_kv_fragment" during merge path. Also higher system time due to page faults: ```
# perf top
40.2% memcpy
12.8% copy_kv_fragment
11.0% kv_pager_reclaim
```

tim: could be that merging forces materialization of KV prefix for each shard, causing duplicates before dedupe. If dedupe happens after allocation we pay for both.

ravinder: proposed fix: update reuse-indexing to maintain indirection map. When merge creates a new batch_key, record mapping from old_keys -> new_key before freeing. Then reuse path can find existing frag and avoid allocation. Also make eviction tolerant to transient aliasing.

marta: we should also add a short-lived quarantine for fragments: when a frag is freed due to a merge, keep it in a fast LRU for X seconds. If reuse requests map to the new key, reassign without realloc. Avoids immediate malloc churn.

sasha: +1. quick mitigation: reduce coalesce threshold to 1 in prod to reduce merge rate until we patch.

oliver: let's add a microbenchmark: many merges + longctx to measure mem delta and p99. I can wire a harness using existing longctx runner.

ravinder: I'll own the indirection map patch. Outline: (1) add batch_alias table: old_key -> canonical_key, (2) on merge populate aliases for both constituent keys, (3) update find_frag to consult alias table before allocating. Also add metrics: alias_hits, alias_misses, frag_alloc_rate.

marta: test plan: unit for aliasing, integration with KV pager under high-concurrency, perf job (10k requests, 60k ctx) comparing mem slope.

sasha: repro steps in case helpful: 
1) start local perf node with coalescer v2 flags
2) run script: ./tools/longctx_runner --profile --seq 60000 --requests 10000 --concurrency 8
3) monitor /metrics kv_frag_alloc_total kv_frag_free_total alias_hits alias_misses

ravinder: I'll send a draft PR after lunch. If anyone sees additional edgecases (split where a batch is later split again), ping me — alias map needs to handle split+merge chains.

marta: also instrument the evictor to log when it evicts fragments that are later referenced within X seconds — that'll show false-evict churn.

sasha: thanks, team. lowering coalesce on prod now and scheduling follow-up sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
